encounters.cc: Six-week history of persistent low mood, early morning awakening, and difficulty concentrating.

lines: Six-week history of persistent low mood, early morning awakening, and difficulty concentrating.
The patient is a 38-year-old female with autoimmune hypothyroidism and primary ovarian insufficiency who returns for follow-up of major depressive disorder initially diagnosed in March 2021.
She was started on sertraline 100 mg daily approximately three months ago with minimal improvement and presents with continued symptoms.
She reports lost interest in activities she once enjoyed, such as hiking and cooking, and finds it difficult to feel excited about anything.
She reports significant sleep disturbances, waking up around 4 a.m. every day and being unable to fall back asleep.
Her appetite is poor, and she has unintentionally lost 10 pounds over the last month.
She feels guilty about being "unproductive" and says she sometimes wonders if her family would be better off without her, although she denies having any active suicidal intent or plan.
She has no history of mania or psychosis.
She has never received psychiatric treatment before and says she is open to therapy "if that helps," but feels too exhausted to find a therapist or attend regular sessions right now.
She denies any recent psychosocial stressors.
She asks if there's something she can take "to help take the edge off" so she can function better.
